svg.title: claudia composes — the object layer and rotating an object in a text
svg.desc: A text in flow view with a stamp and a photo floating over it on an object layer; the stamp held, with the handle and the tether to the character it hangs from; the two layers; what happens when text above changes; menus and keys; open points.
svg.text: claudia composes — an object layer over the text, and turning what floats on it

For review before any code. Content is invented. The model already has floating objects hung from a character (D179, D907); the web client does not draw them yet. This is how they appear, how you reach them, and how they turn.
A · A text with objects floating over it
Flow view. The stamp is held: handle, chip and, new in composes, a dashed tether to the character it hangs from. The text under the stamp does not move or wrap
The second quarter closed with a surplus of 4.1 percent, mostly from lower travel
costs. Two items stand out: the software licences, which are paid once a year, and
the exchange rates used for foreign invoices, which were fixed in January and
have not been looked at since.
Travel was cheaper because the autumn conference moved online. We expect the
saving to hold for one more quarter and then to disappear, since two of the three
teams plan to meet in person again in the spring.
The next step is a review of the rates before the half-year close. Tobi will collect
the invoices, and Anna will check the figures in the table against the sources.
Turning does not touch the anchor,
so the history says only the angle.
The object layer lies over the text and takes the pointer only where an object is;
everywhere else the click is the text's. Esc leaves an object and puts the caret back
→ caret at the anchor / edit its words
The anchor follows the character through other people's edits, as cursors and
suggestions do (D179); the turn and the size stay.
after anna adds a paragraph above
Join the paragraph it hangs from to the one before and the object goes with it; split it
and the objects past the cut go to the new paragraph. On the printed page the turned
outline is what the margins are tested against (D907).
Handle and chip as in mock-up 1: 342°, not −18°.
The tether runs from the frame's top-left corner (dashed grey: the frame as if upright) to the
character the object hangs from. It, the ring on the character and the chip appear only while
the object is held, so reading is quiet.
The corner is the point the model keeps (D907: the object's top-left is where it hangs).
Turning is about the centre, so the corner does not move.
A photo turned 3° in the margin: objects may stand outside the text column; nothing wraps
(D179). It is not held, so it shows no anchor.
The text under a transparent box stays readable and editable; a click on the box's empty middle
holds the box, not the words (open point 3).
The object layer. Objects keep their order (the stacking order of the object model).
The text layer: paragraphs, runs and the carets of the people writing.
Before and after: the stamp moved down with its paragraph and kept its angle.
Menus and keys, new in composes
The same entries and keys as creates and computes (D361).
Format gains Describe Object… and Rotate ▸ (Rotate Right 90°, Rotate Left 90°, Rotate
By…), as in creates and computes; both are greyed unless an object is held. Insert at
the caret: the new object hangs from the character before it, 32 px down and right.
1 A free offset from the anchor
Today the object's corner sits on its character (D179,
D907). To float anywhere, the anchor needs an offset (dx,
dy). Recommended: add it, as this mock-up shows.
Recommended: Select Next Object (above). Tab stays the
